subject: Version guardrails + maintenance sprint plan for Private deployments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Reyes <maya@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Version guardrails + maintenance sprint plan for Private deployments

Team —

I want to lock in a short maintenance sprint for Private (VPC/on-prem) customers to apply the 2026.11 runtime patch and related dependency updates. This thread is to agree on guardrails (what we pin vs allow to float), scheduling windows, and clear rollback criteria so ACME and other enterprise customers can plan. Key constraints we need to accommodate:

- Some customers (Acme) are on strict change freezes until EOD Tues their local time.
- We must preserve existing pinned model artifacts for tenants that requested version pinning.
- Rollback must be automated to a known-good image and KV-cache state; manual DB migrations must be avoidable.

Proposed sprint summary (high level):
1) Preflight: run canary job on dedicated pool with sample workload for 6 hours (non-peak).
2) Window: 3hr rolling windows by region (US: Wed 02:00–05:00 UTC).
3) Guardrails: only permit minor runtime bumps (semver patch/minor) for pinned tenants; UX-level feature flags disabled.
4) Rollback: automated image switch + warm KV cache fallback; revert routing to previous model variant.

I've attached a short PDF with the guardrail checklist and a calendar invite stub. Please review and call out any hard blockers by EOD Monday.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Reyes <maya@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Version guardrails + maintenance sprint plan for Private deployments

Jordan —

Thanks for the starter plan. A few practical notes from the runtime ops side:

- Canary duration: 6 hours is fine, but we should require two independent canaries (one for long-context loads, one for short bursts). This surfaced the last time we swapped kernel selection.
- Rollback automation: we already have an image switcher but KV warm-up is tricky for big tenants. I'd like to add a "cold-traffic" gating period (15m) after rollback where we only allow 25% of traffic routing until cache hit rates recover.
- Binaries & libc changes: if the patch touches libc-level libs, we must treat it as a major and require full revalidation; add that to the guardrail doc.

Also, for customers with pinned models, we should publish a simple manifest that says: runtime version X, model family Y, quantization Z — this makes approval easier on their side.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Reliability Engineer
From: Maya Reyes <maya@acme-cloud.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Version guardrails + maintenance sprint plan for Private deployments

Jordan / Ben / Soojin —

Appreciate the heads-up. A couple items from Acme's side:

- The Tues freeze note means we can't accept anything that changes runtime ABI before Thu 00:00 UTC; can you confirm the proposed US window won't touch that?
- We need the manifest Ben mentioned at least 48 hours before our window to run internal SCC (security/compliance) checks.
- For rollback, our ops want a post-rollback validation script we can run from our side to check request/response latencies and sampling of model outputs (we can share a small harness).

If you can share the manifest and the validation harness by Tue 14:00 UTC we'll be able to sign off.

Thanks,
Maya Reyes
Head of Platform Ops
Acme Cloud
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Reyes <maya@acme-cloud.com>, ops@acme-cloud.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:08:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Version guardrails + maintenance sprint plan for Private deployments

Thanks everyone — quick operational plan below and actions assigned. Keeping it tight so we can meet Acme's timing.

Operational plan (concise):
- Artifact manifest: produce YAML manifest with fields {runtime_version, kernel_profile, model_variant, quantization_profile, bundle_checksum}. Target: Tue 2026-11-24 12:00 UTC. Owner: Marissa.
- Dual canaries: short-burst (5m QPS spike), long-run (6h representative). Owner: Ben (canary configs in ops repo).
- Window: Keep Wed 02:00–05:00 UTC for US. We'll avoid Tue entirely per Acme ask.
- Rollback: image switch + routing rollback script + 15m cold-traffic gate as Ben suggested. Automated smoke-run will emit a status file to S3 and we’ll post a webhook to Acme ops for their harness.
- Failure criteria (any of the following triggers rollback):
  * 5xx increase > 1.5x baseline for 10m
  * 95th latency regression > 200ms above baseline for 10m
  * Model-quality regression on eval set (auto alert)

Attachments: guardrails PDF (v1), tentative calendar ICS for Wed slot, rollback-validation-summary.txt containing the expected smoke checks.

Action items:
- Marissa: manifest by Tue 12:00 UTC + upload to Drive link.
- Ben: finalize canary configs and run canary on our staging dedicated pool Tue 18:00 UTC.
- Jordan: notify top-10 pinned customers with the manifest link once Marissa uploads.

I'll run a 30-minute sync Tues 13:00 UTC to confirm readiness. If no major blockers, we proceed with Wed rolling windows.

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Deployment Ops
Redwood Inference
